exposure: maternal dietary inflammatory index during pregnancy
Maternal dietary inflammatory index (DII) during pregnancy
cohort: 5120 singleton pregnancies from mother-child cohorts in Spain (INfancia y Medio Ambiente), Greece (Rhea), and the United States (Project Viva)
finding: Higher prepregnancy BMI is associated with shorter duration of any and exclusive breastfeeding, with maternal dietary inflammation, systemic inflammation, and mode of delivery being key mediators of this association.
mod_finding: Cesarean delivery mediated the association between prepregnancy BMI and both duration of any breastfeeding (6.54%) and exclusive breastfeeding (7.69%).
